purpose: Resolve apparent shared numeric token 332 across study years before changing the King Rail biological replication unit.

original_article.evidence: Brewer et al. report 14 captures (1 in 2019, 5 in 2020, 8 in 2021) with 10 stabilized home ranges; the authors explicitly state no banded birds were recaptured or observed across years.

parsed_ids.group_unit: source numeric tag token PLUS year
parsed_ids.interpretation: The tag token 332 occurs in two bird-year keys, but no source-documented marked bird persisted across years. Removing '_20' or '_21' would fabricate a biological-individual join and contradict the original article's capture/recapture statement.
parsed_ids.correct_reporting_unit: 10 distinct source bird×year identities consistent with 10 independently marked birds reported by Brewer et al.
parsed_ids.observed_rows: 607 source table records; 190 matched used/random events, 10 original source bird×year IDs.
parsed_ids.mandatory_boundary: Treating shared numeric token alone as demonstrated repeated animal identity is invalid. If a source-specific crosswalk later establishes physical ID reuse, then update only after that independent attestation.

contrast_with_california: The California waterfowl P9ELSUHN source defines birdyear as tagged individual plus agricultural year and documented repeated individual prefixes: its identity hierarchy must NOT be transferred to this independent King Rail archive.
